Abstract: Camrelizumab plus famitinib as first-line treatment for locally advanced or metastatic pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinomas (CAPSTONE): a multi-center, single-arm, phase 2 trial.. BACKGROUND: The combination of immune checkpoint inhibitors and antiangiogenic agents has demonstrated a synergistic antitumor effect in numerous solid tumors, but has rarely been investigated in pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma (PSC). We assessed the activity and safety of camrelizumab (a programmed cell death-1 inhibitor) plus famitinib (an antiangiogenic agent) in patients with PSC. METHODS: CAPSTONE is an open-label, single-arm, Simon two-stage, phase 2 trial done at eight sites in China. data.text: PMID 42964201: "Hepatitis B Immunoprophylaxis rarely prevents molecularly evident subclinical HBV infection in children born to HBsAg-positive mothers." (Front Microbiol, 2026). Abstract: Hepatitis B Immunoprophylaxis rarely prevents molecularly evident subclinical HBV infection in children born to HBsAg-positive mothers.. Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains one of the most life-threatening human pathogens causing chronic hepatitis B and hepatocellular carcinoma in millions of people globally. Protective vaccines are available for decades, but their implementation is not yet universal. Mother-to-child transmission remains the prevailing route of HBV spread. Regardless of antiviral treatment of HBV-infected pregnant woman and neonatal immunoprophylaxis, HBV is transmitted at low levels to newborns as a subclinical (occult) infection at rates ranging from singular cases to the majority of the infant population examined in different centers worldwide. data.text: PMID 42964179: "Incremental diagnostic value of serum progesterone combined with transvaginal ultrasound in differentiating early ectopic pregnancy: a single-center real-world study." (Front Med (Lausanne), 2026). Abstract: Incremental diagnostic value of serum progesterone combined with transvaginal ultrasound in differentiating early ectopic pregnancy: a single-center real-world study.. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate serum progesterone combined with transvaginal ultrasound for distinguishing ectopic pregnancy (EP) in patients with pregnancy of unknown location (PUL), and to assess diagnostic efficacy across risk stratifications. METHODS: Internally unvalidated analysis included 148 PUL patients (January 2022-December 2025). Final diagnosis by surgical pathology or follow-up divided patients into EP (49) and non-EP (99; intrauterine pregnancy or natural regression). All underwent initial transvaginal ultrasound to confirm PUL. The prediction point was the 48-hour reassessment. Predictors were abnormal adnexal findings on follow-up ultrasound at 48 h, serum progesterone, and 48-hour β-hCG results available at that visit.
